content: The WHO Guidelines for Malaria underwent several updates between February 2021 and October 2023, consolidating all current recommendations into a single, user-friendly online resource. These guidelines include evidence-based recommendations for malaria prevention (such as vector control and preventive chemotherapies), case management (diagnosis and treatment), and elimination strategies, with links to additional resources like operational manuals, surveillance tools, and glossaries. Key Updates: 1. February 16, 2021: The guidelines were consolidated for the first time, bringing together all WHO recommendations for malaria prevention and case management. Recommendations for elimination settings were noted as under development. 2. July 13, 2021: Updates were made to the vector control guidance: A systematic review on larval habitat modification and manipulation found insufficient evidence to recommend these interventions, highlighting evidence gaps requiring further research. A conditional recommendation for house screening was introduced based on a systematic review of housing modifications. Background information was added on how insecticide-treated nets (ITNs) protect both individual users and the community, emphasizing the community effect. Sections on insecticide resistance management clarified that data from resistance assays should not guide the selection of pyrethroid products. Resource estimates for WHO-recommended interventions were added to support local cost-effectiveness studies and intervention package selection. 3. February 18, 2022: The first-ever WHO recommendation on a malaria vaccine was included, based on a comprehensive evidence review of the RTS,S/AS01 vaccine and advice from the Malaria Policy Advisory Group (MPAG) and the Strategic Advisory Group of Experts (SAGE) on Immunization. 4. March 31, 2022: Revisions to vector control guidance included: Updates to the conditional recommendation for deploying pyrethroid-PBO nets, based on a revised systematic review. New recommendations for deploying pyrethroid-only long-lasting insecticidal nets (LLINs), pyrethroid-PBO nets, and indoor residual spraying (IRS) in areas affected by humanitarian emergencies. Expanded details on insecticide selection for IRS, emphasizing the risks of using DDT and the importance of alternative insecticides. Additional information on resource considerations, costs, and cost-effectiveness for WHO-recommended interventions. Updates on evidence gaps and research needs for malaria vector control. 5. June 13, 2022: Updates were made to malaria chemoprevention recommendations, including: Intermittent preventive treatment during pregnancy (IPTp). Perennial malaria chemoprevention (PMC), previously referred to as intermittent preventive treatment in infants (IPTi). Seasonal malaria chemoprevention (SMC). New recommendations for intermittent preventive treatment in school-aged children (IPTsc), post-discharge malaria chemoprevention (PDMC), mass drug administration (MDA) for burden and transmission reduction, and mass relapse prevention. The first WHO recommendations for interventions in the final phase of malaria elimination and prevention of re-establishment were introduced, based on evidence reviews of mass testing and treatment, targeted testing and treatment, reactive drug administration, and reactive case detection and treatment. 6. November 25, 2022: Updates to case management included: The addition of new molecules for treating uncomplicated malaria. Optimization of dosage regimens for anti-relapse treatment. Updates on the use of antimalarial medicines in special risk populations, including pregnant women. 7. March 14, 2023: New WHO recommendations were introduced for two classes of insecticide-treated nets: Pyrethroid-chlorfenapyr ITNs. Pyrethroid-pyriproxyfen ITNs. Separate guidance was developed for prioritizing ITN products under resource-constrained conditions, given the increasing complexity of resource allocation. 8. October 16, 2023: The latest update included: Revised information on the use of indoor residual spraying (IRS) for malaria prevention. A conditional recommendation against the use of topical repellents for community-level malaria control. These updates were informed by recent systematic reviews and a technical consultation on comparative efficacy assessments, including data on the new insecticide broflanilide for IRS. While the recommendations themselves remained unchanged, revised evidence profiles replaced older reviews, providing more detailed information on how recommendations were formulated. Practical guidance on the interventions was also added, and broflanilide was included as an insecticide under the WHO IRS recommendation for malaria control. These updates reflect WHO's commitment to refining malaria control and elimination strategies based on the latest evidence and expert consultations.
